qualifications_or_emphasis: The Company has received notices from BSE & NSE imposing fine of Rs. 2,14,760/- (inclusive of GST) each for non-compliance with Regulation 17(1A) of SEBI LODR Regulations due to change in designation of Shri Rikhab Chand Jain (who has attained the age of 75 years) from Executive Director & Chairman to Non-Executive Director & Chairman w.e.f April 01, 2025, without prior approval of Shareholders. The Company has paid the fines and taken the approval of shareholders in the AGM held on 24th September, 2025.

The composition of the Audit Committee was not in compliance with Regulation 18(1)(b) of the SEBI LODR Regulations for the period from May 21, 2025 to August 06, 2025, as the Audit Committee comprised five members including two Executive Directors and three Independent Directors. The Company identified this non-compliance pursuant to observations received from BSE and NSE on the Integrated Governance Report filed for the quarter ended June 30, 2025. Subsequently, the Company inducted one additional Independent Director on the Audit Committee with effect from August 07, 2025 and reconstituted the Committee to ensure compliance with the aforementioned Regulation.

outlook.statement: The outlook for TT Limited remains highly optimistic as the Company enters a new phase of strategic growth following a comprehensive business transformation aligned with its Vision 2030 roadmap. The Company aims to rebuild and significantly scale its top line through aggressive expansion across domestic and international markets, with domestic business driven by deeper penetration of brands in innerwear, casual wear, and active wear segments, and export segment poised to emerge as a key growth driver supported by FTAs and MMF textiles competitiveness. The newly commissioned garment manufacturing facility in Howrah is expected to stabilize and contribute meaningfully. The Company plans to diversify into allied segments such as packaging solutions with a corrugated carton manufacturing unit. With a strengthened balance sheet, reduced debt levels, and improved financial flexibility, the Company is well-positioned to invest in growth initiatives, innovation, and strategic partnerships. Supportive government policies including PLI schemes are expected to provide a conducive environment. The Company is confident of achieving consistent double-digit growth in the medium to long term.
The Company commenced Commercial production in its New Factory in Howrah, West Bengal in the month of July 2025.

Going forward, the Company aims to rebuild and significantly scale its top line through aggressive expansion across domestic and international markets. The domestic business is expected to witness strong growth driven by deeper penetration of the Company's brands in innerwear, casual wear, and active wear segments across traditional retail, modern trade, and e-commerce platforms. The export segment is poised to emerge as a key growth driver, supported by favorable global trade dynamics, including Free Trade Agreements with key markets and India's increasing competitiveness in man-made fibre (MMF) textiles. The newly commissioned garment manufacturing facility in Howrah is expected to stabilize and contribute meaningfully to operational performance in the coming periods. Additionally, the Company is exploring expansion opportunities within textile clusters such as PM MITRA Parks, which will provide scale efficiencies and ecosystem advantages.
